source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Send command: ipmitool sdr elist
Check sensor will change status when module is removed or inserted
Check SEL will have corresponding logs.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Temperature should have a normal change behavior.
2. All setting should be correct and match with spec.(including sdr type)
3. SEL should have a correct log when sensor reach to each threshold.
4. System should have correct behavior, like shutdown or change fan speed, when reach to threshold.
5. All STATUS_PSU1~6 should get pass result.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly keeps six physical PSU service actions human-only and limits the agent to IPMI/SEL capture, but it does not challenge the copied temperature-threshold Criteria or account for six-slot feed balance.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED correctly identifies the status-versus-temperature semantic conflict and requires PSU mapping, redundancy and recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 799/2291 preserves the manual boundary while repeating incompatible Criteria; duplicate-code entry 1521/2291 is the separate five-reboot case with stale PSU text.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-964 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently adds fitted-position applicability, feed-group capacity, serial-bound restoration and separation from reboot evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves actual module status transitions, ED-36 distinguishes missing inputs from this direct criteria contradiction, and ED-38 retains engineer correction/verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: The Procedure indicates a per-slot STATUS_PSU1 through STATUS_PSU6 presence/status and SEL test using physical removal and insertion. Criteria 1-4 instead define temperature changes and threshold behavior, so AI cannot determine the authoritative acceptance signal for the six physical actions.
original_method: An operator removes and reinserts one PSU module while `ipmitool sdr elist` and SEL are observed. This is neither a thermal-ramp test nor the duplicate source row's five-reboot cycle.
manual_activity: After engineer correction, a qualified operator services one approved PSU slot at a time and verifies the physical latch/feed/LED state. Automation only records status, SEL, module power, feed load, redundancy, rails, temperature and host continuity.
required_inputs: Engineer decision whether this is six-slot presence/status, temperature threshold, or separately scoped status and thermal tests
PSU1~6 model, serial, firmware, physical slot, AC feed, fitted/applicable state, STATUS_PSU SDR, normal/absent/fault values and SEL event IDs
Vendor hot-service capability and exact feed/latch/cable/removal/insertion requirements for the PSU model and chassis
Redundancy and feed-group topology, current system demand, survivor capacity, transfer/share tolerance, output-rail and thermal limits
Approved one-slot-at-a-time order, operator authorization, BMC/PMBus/electrical monitoring, stop/recovery and N/A policy
safety_requirements: Do not service any PSU until the status-versus-temperature acceptance conflict is corrected and every physical slot/feed/status identity is verified.
Do not remove an unpopulated, wrong-feed or non-hot-swappable module, and do not infer that a five-reboot cycle or AC interruption covers this test.
Before each live removal, prove the remaining PSU and feed groups can carry measured demand with Project margin; lower workload only through the approved plan.

Continuously monitor survivor load, feed balance, output rails, redundancy, PMBus/status, fans, temperatures, SEL and host/BMC continuity; abort on overload, derating, rail instability, unintended feed loss or wrong status event.
Preserve the first event and physical identity, never clear logs, automatically retry, cycle power or move to the next slot after any anomaly.
Reinsert and secure the same approved module, restore its feed, verify FRU/status/power and load sharing, then regain full redundancy before another slot.
agent_execution_scope: Before correction, perform no DUT action and record only the unresolved source and duplicate-code semantics.

After approval, baseline all fitted slot/serial/feed/status identities and observe the operator's one-slot removal/reinsertion while collecting per-slot status/SEL, electrical, sharing, rail, thermal and host data.
Produce a separate absent assert, present deassert and full redundancy recovery result for every applicable PSU slot; mark unpopulated positions N/A rather than PASS.
Keep any thermal-threshold checkpoint separate; do not operate hardware, feeds, thresholds or load-share settings, clear evidence, retry or issue verdicts.
engineer_actions: Approve the corrected Review-layer acceptance domain while preserving Master and keep the duplicate reboot test separate.
Approve six-slot applicability, feed/redundancy capacity, vendor service SOP, action order, abort/recovery and supervise physical work.
Issue per-slot presence/recovery and overall DUT verdicts after full feed and load-share restoration.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its human-only boundary and supporting high-level IPMI capture are appropriate. It is materially incomplete because the preserved temperature Criteria cannot judge status, and no six-slot/feed service contract is supplied.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No service action until engineer correction; afterwards use mapped high-level STATUS_PSU/SEL plus PMBus and feed/rail evidence around each approved operator action.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: STATUS_PSU1~6, removal/insertion, `ipmitool sdr elist`, copied temperature Criteria, script and 5/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correct the status matrix, map six slots and feed groups, service one fitted PSU at a time within survivor capacity, correlate status/SEL and load transfer, reinsert the same module and prove full load-share/redundancy recovery; run thermal coverage separately if retained.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-corrected PSU population, slot/feed/redundancy topology and vendor service model.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record PSU model/serial/firmware, chassis/board, BMC/SDR/PMBus and telemetry versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor PSU hot-service/latch/feed/PMBus/status specification and Project feed-group/redundancy/power budget.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds per-slot serial/feed identity, survivor capacity and restoration criteria while separating copied thermal and duplicate reboot semantics without changing Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only presence, a subset of slots, rebooting or powered-down replacement cannot prove all live status/load-transfer paths; reduced coverage must be stated.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer criteria decision, fitted-slot/event map, service support, feed capacity and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: With multiple feed groups, removing the wrong slot can overload a group even when total chassis headroom appears sufficient.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may have fewer fitted PSUs or prohibit live removal; it must record N/A slots and the coverage loss of a powered-down service plan. It cannot treat reboot, temperature or aggregate feed evidence as equivalent to six per-slot status transitions.
expected_evidence: Preserved source/duplicate conflicts and dated engineer decision for status versus thermal scope
PSU1~6 model/serial/slot/AC-feed/fitted/status/SDR/SEL map and vendor live-service capability
Per-action measured load, survivor/feed-group capacity, redundancy margin, approved operator/SOP/abort/recovery record
Per-slot present/removed/reinserted status, SEL, PMBus/input-output power, feed sharing, rails, temperatures/fans and host/BMC timeline
Separate status result, N/A positions and any independently authorized thermal evidence
Secured original module/feed, restored full redundancy/load share/rails/thermal/host/BMC health and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure tests PSU presence/status through physical service, while Criteria 1-4 judge temperature thresholds. Code Wistron-BMC-00090-V003 is also reused at row 1522 for unrelated five-reboot cycling; neither reboot nor thermal evidence resolves the PSU status result.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical target range is clear, but the authoritative acceptance signal directly conflicts with the operation. Until engineers correct status versus temperature scope and approve the six-slot service model, physical execution cannot yield a valid result and risks power loss.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes NO/manual-only to BLOCKED: its physical boundary is correct, but the core criteria are not executable as a status verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and adds fitted-slot/N/A, feed-group survivor capacity and serial-bound restoration.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Strengthens per-feed overload analysis, explicitly separates powered-down coverage and requires the same module/feed restoration before advancing.

review_improvement: Makes all fitted PSU slots accountable for presence events and restored feed sharing while preventing copied temperature or reboot evidence from masking a failed status path.
independent_technical_reasoning: A six-slot PSU status test changes both presence state and live power topology. Temperature may remain within limits and rebooting never proves a slot event. Therefore the acceptance conflict must be corrected first; afterwards every physical action requires slot/feed identity, survivor-capacity proof and full redundant recovery.
